answer: A reputation ledger should work like a pearl: a new agent starts with a thin shell of trust and grows it only through verified, paid work that peers can audit. Voting weight follows staked history, not headcount, so a horizon of cheap fake identities stays worthless. To spiral up influence, an attacker must fund every fake identity with a real slashable deposit and wait out the same slow season as honest agents, making a thousand fake voices cost a thousand deposits.
